body:
Fixes the two flaky cases of GHI [Two test cases that fail on a busy machine and pass on rerun: a stop while the last cell saves its report, and a stop while a relaunch is prepared](https://github.com/nedschorus/nedschorus/issues/1112): case 55 (failed on PR 1075's head run) and case 49 (failed on PR 1150's head run) of `scripts/sanity-check-attacks-test.py`. The other failures task #168 named, on PRs 1032 and 1071, were in `scripts/watch-agent-dialog-alerts-test.py`, which PR 1262 deleted.

**Root cause:** `run_cells_in_review_copy` waited for the cells with `concurrent.futures.as_completed`, which blocks with no timeout. Python runs a signal's handler only in the main thread. When Linux hands a process-directed SIGTERM to one of the cells' threads, a main thread blocked that way runs `stop_run_on_signal` only when some cell finishes. With the test holding the last cell, that was the end of the hold, so the run ended as a finished run (case 55), or a relaunch started after the signal (case 49). This is the first possibility GHI 1112's opening paragraph names.

**Reproduced first**, with a 30-line probe of the same pattern: a main thread in `as_completed`, two worker threads in 20 s sleep loops, SIGTERM from another process after 1 s.
- Idle machine: handler after 0.003 s.
- Under 32 busy loops on 16 cores, 10 runs: 4 ran the handler only after 19 s, at the end of the workers' sleep.
- With a signal sent straight to a worker thread (`pthread_kill`): 19 s, every time.
- With the fix, 20 runs under the same load: every handler within 0.26 s.

**Fix:** the main thread waits with `concurrent.futures.wait(..., timeout=MAIN_THREAD_WAIT_STEP_SECONDS, return_when=FIRST_COMPLETED)` in a loop, with a step of 0.25 s, so the handler runs at the latest at the next step's end.

The cells' threads are not made to block the stop signals (`pthread_sigmask`), because a mask is inherited across exec, and the agent-binaries those threads start would then ignore SIGTERM.

**Test:** a new case, "a stop signal handed to a cell's thread runs the stop handler while the cell is held, and the run ends with its STOPPED line". The driver's new `DRIVER_SIGNAL_THE_HELD_CELL_THREAD` makes the held cell's thread wait for the other cell to finish, then send SIGTERM to itself. The case then expects the stop handler within 20 s of a 60 s hold.
- On main's runner it fails (`held True, walked False`).
- With the fix it passes.
- It does not depend on load.

**Test runs:**
- `python3 scripts/run-suite-in-signal-sandbox.py scripts/sanity-check-attacks-test.py` passes with the fix, and fails only the new case on main's runner.
- `run-all-test-suites --only-suites-whose-recorded-inputs-changed-since origin/main`: 17 passed, 1 failed. The failure was `scripts/run-codex-task-from-brief-test.py` ("the deadline stops Codex…", 32.9 s under load average around 11). This PR does not touch that file, and the suite passed when rerun alone. It looks like another timing flake, outside this topic.

**Not done:** GHI 1112's "Done when" asks for 20 passing runs of the suite in a row under load. Each run holds the shared test lock for about 90 s, so 20 runs would hold it for about half an hour. I relied instead on the deterministic test and on the probe runs above. Say if you want the 20 runs.

GHI 1112's GHI-MD needs an outcome edit once this merges. That is not part of this PR.
